effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

changes.historical_text: If this face-up card is returned from the field to your Deck, select and Special Summon 1 Level 3 or lower monster from your Deck to your side of the field. Then shuffle your Deck.
changes.summary: Period procedure only, not a text erratum: both scripts fire the mandatory return-to-Deck trigger without checking that a Level 3 or lower monster remains in the Deck (s.sptg is `return true` in each), but the GOAT script proves a failed search by revealing the Deck (Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)) where the modern script silently does nothing. That single else-branch is the entire script difference.

review.notes: Cleanest case in the batch: the GOAT variant's database text is character-identical to the modern cdb text and both equal lineage v1 (DB2-EN167), and the script diff is nothing but the Duel.GoatConfirm else-branch - so this is component (A) alone, with no relaxed activation condition to leave undated and no flag needed. v0 (LOD-057, 2003, 'returned directly from the field') and v2 (OP25-EN013, 2024, 'shuffled from the field into your Deck') are cosmetic; both scripts implement the trigger identically as EVENT_TO_DECK with IsPreviousPosition(POS_FACEUP) and IsPreviousLocation(LOCATION_ONFIELD). Minor note, not an era mismatch: the baseline text v1 was first printed 2005-07-27, about four months after the GOAT snapshot date, but it is behaviourally identical to v0, which was in print from 2003.
